record.paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Give a complete characterization of the signed graphs Σ whose edge sets can be decomposed into positive circles.

evidence.quote: Qn. 10+. Which Σ can be decomposed into positive circles? Ans. Partially known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair Σ = (G, σ) where G = (V, E) is a finite graph (loops and multiple edges allowed) and σ : E → {+1, −1} is a labeling of the edges by signs. A circle (also called a cycle or circuit) of Σ is the edge set of a connected 2-regular subgraph of G. The sign of a circle C is the product σ(C) = ∏_{e ∈ C} σ(e); the circle C is called positive if σ(C) = +1 and negative otherwise. A decomposition of the edge set E into positive circles is a partition of E into pairwise edge-disjoint subsets E₁, …, E_k such that each E_i is a positive circle of Σ.

Problem: Give a complete characterization of all signed graphs Σ whose edge set E admits a decomposition into positive circles.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as a problem with only a partially known answer in Zaslavsky's problem collection on signed graph circles. Web search did not surface a complete characterization; relevant results discuss only special subclasses (e.g., chordal signed graphs, matroid-theoretic descriptions of single circuits). The general characterization appears to remain open.
